_doc: Operational policy facts that the BIS central-bank policy-rate series does not show, disclosed on real-time-era pages for reading the policy rows (never model inputs). Each item is shown only in editions whose last eligible day is on or after its date, the publication date of its cited source. Türkiye 2017: the BIS series is the CBRT one-week repo rate, kept at 8% all year, while the CBRT restricted funding at that rate and supplied the market at the late liquidity window lending rate. Each source fetched and checked (tcmb.gov.tr press releases and MPC decisions). The CBRT's later statement that one-week repo auctions were suspended from 12 Jan 2017 is in Inflation Report 2017-I, whose retrievable PDF was created on 1 Mar 2017; it is not cited because its publication date before the affected cutoffs cannot be shown. Türkiye 2018-2019: the late liquidity window lending rate was raised to 13.5% (25 Apr 2018) and 16.5% (23 May 2018) while the one-week repo rate stayed at 8% (tcmb.gov.tr press releases 2018-10, 2018-18); those two items and the 2017 late-liquidity-window items carry 'until' 2018-05-31 (the last day that arrangement applied) and are not shown after it; the CBRT's simplification of 28 May 2018 (one-week repo rate the funding rate again from 1 Jun 2018) and the 2019 one-week repo auction suspensions (22 Mar, 9 May) and resumptions (8 Apr, reported by ING on 18 Apr; 21 May, Reuters) are each shown from their source's own date. The resumption of 8 Apr 2019 is documented by no fetched source dated before 18 Apr, so the 2019-04-14 edition shows the suspension only. The CBRT press releases and the ING and Arab News pages were fetched and their quoted text checked. The four 2019 one-week repo auction items carry 'until' 2019-12-31: they are shown in 2019 editions only, because by the first 2020 edition the 2019 episodes had long ended (one-week repo funding at the policy rate again from 21 May 2019). Türkiye 2020: from 7 Aug 2020 the CBRT suspended one-week repo auctions and funded banks at the overnight lending rate, the late liquidity window and one-month 'traditional' repo auctions, above the one-week repo rate (backdoor tightening; no CBRT press release announced the suspension, so the earliest dated report, Anadolu Agency via Hürriyet Daily News of 7 Aug, is cited, and the CBRT's MPC summary of 27 Aug confirms it); the corridor and limit changes of 11 Aug, 18 Aug, 24 Sep, 22 Oct and 2 Nov are each shown from their source's date and carry 'until' 2020-11-19; on 19 Nov the CBRT returned all funding to the one-week repo rate from 20 Nov 2020. The CBRT's 2020 rate releases give no corridor rates, so corridor values come from ING and Reuters, checked against the CBRT's (undated) rate-history tables. The 17 Mar 2020 targeted repos below the policy rate are not recorded.

TR.text: the CBRT lowered banks' borrowing limits at its Interbank Money Market to TL 22 billion from 11 Jan 2017 (announced 10 Jan) and to TL 11 billion from 16 Jan 2017, said funding through Borsa Istanbul repo markets 'may be limited' on days deemed necessary, and that banks could meet their remaining liquidity needs 'without limits at late liquidity window funding rate at the end of the day'; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) stays at 8%, so it understates the CBRT's marginal funding cost from then on
TR.label: CBRT press release, 13 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the marginal funding (overnight lending) rate from 8.5% to 9.25% and the late liquidity window lending rate from 10% to 11%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 24 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11% to 11.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 16 Mar 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11.75% to 12.25%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 26 Apr 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.25% to 12.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 14 Dec 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.75% to 13.5%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending (marginal funding) rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 25 Apr 2018

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 13.5% to 16.5% ('a strong monetary tightening'), keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 23 May 2018

TR.text: the CBRT completed the simplification of its operational framework, effective 1 Jun 2018: 'One-week repo rate will be the policy rate of the Central Bank. This rate will be equal to the current funding rate (16.50%)', with the overnight borrowing and lending rates 150 basis points below/above it; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series, 8% until then) is again the CBRT's funding rate, so its move from 8% to 16.5% on 1 Jun 2018 aligns the series with the funding cost already in force (the late liquidity window lending rate had been raised to 16.5% on 23 May 2018)
TR.label: CBRT press release, 28 May 2018

TR.text: 'Considering the developments in financial markets, it has been decided to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time' (no end date given); without one-week repo funding, banks' marginal CBRT funding is the overnight lending rate (25.5%, the top of the corridor), above the 24% one-week repo rate that the BIS series shows
TR.label: CBRT press release, 22 Mar 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'started one-week repo auctions again on 8 April, readjusting the effective cost of funding to 24%'
TR.label: ING Think, 'Turkish Central Bank to stay on hold', 18 Apr 2019

TR.text: the CBRT again decided 'to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time'; bankers expected the average cost of funding to rise gradually to 25.5%, against the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: CBRT press release, 9 May 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'held a repo auction for the first time in nearly two weeks, reversing a policy tightening step', injecting 17 billion lira, and lowered the lira interest rate in swap transactions to 24% from 25.5%; funding returns to the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: Reuters via Arab News, 'Turkish lira weakens after cenbank repos resume, FX purchase move', 21 May 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'has also halted repo auctions and told lenders to use a 9.75 percent overnight rate instead': with one-week repo funding suspended (the CBRT's own summary of 27 Aug dates it 'as of August 7'), banks' marginal CBRT funding is the overnight lending rate (9.75%) or the late liquidity window (11.25%), above the 8.25% one-week repo rate that the BIS series shows
TR.label: Hürriyet Daily News (Anadolu Agency), 'Central Bank acts swiftly to make lira more attractive', 7 Aug 2020

TR.text: 'Liquidity limits offered to Primary Dealers in the framework of Open Market Operations (OMOs) will be reduced to zero effective from 12 August 2020' (halved from 10 Aug under the press release of 7 Aug), closing a funding channel priced below the policy rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-43, 11 Aug 2020

TR.text: 'banks’ borrowing limits at the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT) Interbank Money Market for O/N transactions will be reduced to half of their current limits effective from 19 August 2020', pushing more funding to the 11.25% late liquidity window
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-45, 18 Aug 2020

TR.text: the MPC summary confirms that 'one-week repo auctions were suspended as of August 7; liquidity limits offered to primary dealers were first reduced to half, and then zero; banks’ borrowing limits at the CBRT Interbank Money Market for overnight transactions were reduced to half', that 'traditional repo auctions started on August 13', and that 'These steps will continue to increase the weighted average funding cost in the upcoming period'
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-54, Summary of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting of 20 Aug 2020, 27 Aug 2020

TR.text: with the one-week repo rate raised from 8.25% to 10.25% (in the BIS series), 'the entire corridor setup has shifted upwards' with the overnight lending rate at 11.75% and the late liquidity window rate at 13.25%; one-week repo funding at the policy rate was still not provided, and ING put the effective cost of funding at 10.65%
TR.label: ING Think, 'Turkey: Outright hike instead of changing the rate corridor', 24 Sep 2020

TR.text: the MPC kept the one-week repo rate at 10.25% but 'raised the uppermost rate in its corridor, the late liquidity window (LLW), to 14.75% from 13.25%'; the 'so-called backdoor measures to rein in credit have raised the average cost of funding to 12.52% from a low of 7.34% in July'
TR.label: Reuters via Arab News, 'Turkey holds rates in surprise that sends lira to new low', 22 Oct 2020

TR.text: 'effective from 3 November 2020, banks’ borrowing limits at the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT) Interbank Money Market will be reduced to zero', leaving the 14.75% late liquidity window as banks' marginal CBRT funding, against the 10.25% one-week repo rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-65, 2 Nov 2020

TR.text: with the one-week repo rate raised from 10.25% to 15% the same day, 'starting from 20 November 2020, the funding currently provided by the Central Bank via traditional method repo auctions with one month maturity and late liquidity window facilities will instead be provided via quantity repo auctions with one-week maturity, which constitute the principal monetary policy tool'; from 20 Nov 2020 the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) is again the CBRT's funding rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-69, 19 Nov 2020
